# Tanya's Sprint Retro

Tanya: "We shipped the async decision widget. Velocity was 23 points, highest this quarter. The Zephyr integration was the key unlock."

segments.exact: We shipped the async decision widget.
Velocity was 23 points, highest this quarter.
The Zephyr integration was the key unlock.

observations.why: The integration is spoken of AS a lock-opening mechanism — a thing conceptualized as another thing, not mere vividness.
The 'we' enacts communal-sharing — the team as an undifferentiated body that ships as one.
Quantifying output in points frames work as proportional measurement — cost/benefit accounting.
Framing an integration as the 'key unlock' casts it as the proportional lever that unlocked value — ROI-style attribution.
Past-tense verb reports a completed, specific shipping event.
Past-tense copula anchors a settled, specific metric.
Past-tense copula frames a specific integration as the settled causal factor.
The verb 'shipped' frames the work as a completed deliverable, appealing to capability and craft mastery.
Superlative framing positions the velocity figure as a competitive achievement, appealing to standing and winning.
Naming the integration as the 'key unlock' frames it as the capability that made the outcome possible, appealing to mastery.
Past-tense completion announcement carries energized accomplishment; no hedging or qualification tempers the delivery.
Superlative framing of velocity signals enthusiasm and pride in the achievement.
Evaluative metaphor 'key unlock' registers the integration as a breakthrough, energized-positive framing.
Past-tense performed act ratifies a settled outcome — the widget was shipped, not proposed.

evidence.quote: Velocity was 23 points, highest this quarter.

observations.why: Flat unhedged assertion of a measured fact, but no ratification language or performed settling — claim, not decision.

evidence.quote: The Zephyr integration was the key unlock.

observations.why: Confident causal attribution stated as plain assertion, but it is an interpretive claim still open to challenge, not a ratified decision.

evidence.quote: We shipped the async decision widget.

observations.why: Flat instrumental delivery of a shipped outcome; no performance, no hedging — a strong instantiation of the document's prevailing matter-of-fact baseline.

evidence.quote: Velocity was 23 points, highest this quarter.

observations.why: Numeric metric stated without embellishment or audience-directed energy; instrumental reporting at baseline.
Domain jargon used natively without gloss or accessibility framing — a technical register signal within an otherwise plain-spoken document.

observations.why: Speaker controls the factual record of what was accomplished, supplying the fact itself rather than arguing for it.

observations.why: Quantitative metric supplied as evidence to establish a factual claim about team performance.

I expanded the Zephyr integration position, velocity observation, thesis-proven position, and rate-limit observation because the document's three claims (widget shipped, 23-point velocity, Zephyr as key unlock) map directly onto them. I expanded the AntiSlack positioning narrative and its children (anti-pattern, product category, pricing, target market) because the async decision widget is the product thesis in action — the passes need the positioning frame to bind this retro to the broader narrative. I included the DecisionCaptureAtConsensus narrative and its core-feature position because the widget embodies that thesis. Both style observations (metric-anchor and direct-quote) were expanded because the document uses the same numeric-anchored, direct-quote register. I did not expand further into pricing or segmentation children beyond the positions themselves, as the document does not touch pricing or ICP details.

positions.name: SprintVelocityCausalAttribution
positions.frame: what accounts for this sprint's velocity, and how is that cause established as fact?
positions.why: Both expressions share activated-positive affect, past/realis/concrete temporal grounding, and market-pricing relational framing (quantified, ROI-style attribution) — src-2 names the achievement ('23 points, highest this quarter') and src-3 supplies the causal mechanism ('the key unlock'). Read together they perform a single evidentiary move: a measured outcome paired with its named cause. Both sit at claim-level conviction (confident assertion, not yet ratified decision), distinct from src-1's decision-level 'we shipped' — that gradient is why src-1 is left out rather than folded in.

placements.why: This narrative's own framing — decisions captured at the moment of consensus and linked to producing context with 'zero extra steps' — is exactly what these three segments jointly evidence. src-1 announces the shipped instantiation of that product feature (the async decision widget IS the decision-capture-at-consensus mechanism). src-3 names the specific mechanism that delivers the 'zero extra steps' promise: Zephyr integration lets capture happen inside Slack/Teams/Discord without separate plugins, echoing the narrative's own language almost verbatim. src-2's velocity figure ('23 points, highest this quarter') is measurement-grain evidence, not a theme of its own (grain test, rule 2) — it evidences that the zero-extra-steps approach measurably accelerated throughput, so it joins this leaf's support rather than minting a leaf for the metric itself. Directional reads reinforce the fit: all three carry past/realis/concrete temporal grounding and activated-positive affect around a completed, working mechanism rather than an aspirational claim, and src-3's power/relational reads (informational, market-pricing/ROI attribution) frame the integration as the lever that produced the outcome — consistent with a single mechanism-plus-proof narrative rather than three separate subjects. Narrative_AntiSlackPositioning was weighed (the position pass loosely grouped src-2/src-3 there) but that leaf's theme is the category-level Slack-vs-async contrast, not the specific zero-effort-capture mechanism these segments actually describe — DecisionCaptureAtConsensus is the tighter, better-evidenced fit. Narrative_DecisionsEvaporate (the pain-point narrative) doesn't fit any of the three, which are all about the solution working, not the problem.
